goal: A headless supervised autopilot entrypoint runs the daemon outside the console under the shared crash-loop policy, restarting a daemon that dies once inside its window and adopting an already-live daemon via the liveness record so it never spawns a duplicate.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_autopilot_run.py -- main()/run_daemon_loop is the headless daemon with NO supervisor today; the supervised entrypoint wraps the daemon under the shared policy
packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_autopilot_supervisor.py -- the console supervision shape (spawn/respawn/budget) the headless path reuses so console and headless enforce ONE policy
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_autopilot_supervised_run.py -- the new test surface (also used by autopilot-liveness-record); keep both files' suites green
constraints: Reuse the shared policy (supervision-policy-core) and the liveness record (autopilot-liveness-record) -- the headless path must enforce the SAME budget/window and the SAME adoption semantics as the console supervisor, not a parallel implementation.

On adoption: if a live liveness record exists, the headless entrypoint adopts it and spawns no second daemon (spawn count == 0). On a dead daemon inside budget: restart it and continue (a subsequent cycle runs).
Tests must inject the spawn and the clock so respawn and adoption are deterministic, not wall-clock or real-subprocess dependent.
Preserve the daemon's SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful-shutdown and orphan-free exit; the supervised wrapper must not leave an orphan on stop.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not change the existing `flywheel autopilot` daemon's per-cycle behavior or the --once single-pass path.
Do not auto-start autopilot where it was previously manual-start-only; this adds a supervised RUN path, it does not change the cold-start default.
Do not modify or weaken existing autopilot/CLI tests.
Do not introduce a process-manager dependency or a new persistent schema table.
edge_cases: Daemon dies once then succeeds: must be restarted and run a further cycle (proves restart, not just 'entrypoint exists').
An already-live daemon (fresh liveness record) present at startup: the headless entrypoint adopts it and spawns nothing.
Budget exhausted headless: the entrypoint stops respawning and exits/reports the DEAD-after-budget terminal state rather than looping forever.
